JemRec records through Android\'s debugging tools, so USB debugging and Wireless debugging stay on for as long as it is installed. If either is turned off, JemRec turns it back on.

While they are on, a computer paired with this phone can connect to it on the same Wi-Fi, and one you have allowed before can connect over a cable. To switch debugging off for good, uninstall JemRec first.

When it answers, your microphone is muted and your greeting plays to the caller, then a beep. Their message is saved like any recording, marked as a message, and a notification tells you. While they speak you can still take the call: Talk to them in the notification, or unmute on the call screen.

It answers phone calls only - not WhatsApp, Telegram, Viber or Google Meet calls - and never while you are on another call, a messenger call or in a meeting, or roaming, or for a day after you call an emergency number. If JemRec cannot tell who is calling, it lets the phone ring.

JemRec records your greeting the way it records calls, through its recorder, so it never needs permission to use the microphone. Experimental: tested on two phones, an Honor on 2G calls and a Galaxy S23 over Wi-Fi Calling. The test call here is how to know it works on yours.
Best: someone calls you. The next call in three minutes is answered with a short tone and your greeting, whoever is calling - then you are asked whether they heard it.
Someone calling you is a test again from %1$s, a day after your emergency call: until then, the caller may be them calling back.
Or JemRec calls a number that answers by itself, such as your carrier\'s information line, and measures what it can.
